title: Hypergraph Structure
content: Defines `Hypergraph V` as a structure with a single field `edges : Set (Finset V)`. Each hyperedge is a finite set of vertices, and the collection of all edges is a `Set`. This is the most general definition: no restriction on edge sizes, vertex coverage, or multiplicity. Unlike simple graphs where edges are pairs, hyperedges can contain arbitrarily many vertices.
mathContext: A hypergraph $H = (V, E)$ where $E \subseteq 2^V$ is a family of finite subsets of vertices. Formalized as `edges : \text{Set}\;(\text{Finset}\;V)$.

title: k-Uniform Hypergraph
content: Defines `IsUniform H k`: every hyperedge has exactly $k$ vertices. For $k = 2$ this recovers ordinary graphs, and $k = 3$ gives 3-uniform hypergraphs (triple systems). Uniformity is a natural constraint in extremal hypergraph theory, analogous to studying $k$-regular graphs.
mathContext: $H$ is $k$-uniform iff $\forall e \in E(H),\; |e| = k$. For this problem, $k = 3$: every edge is a triple $\{u, v, w\}$.

title: Vertex Degree
content: Defines `degree H v` as the number of hyperedges containing vertex $v$, using `Set.ncard` (cardinality of a possibly infinite set). Marked `noncomputable` because counting elements of a `Set` requires classical choice. The degree function generalizes graph degree to hypergraphs.
mathContext: $\deg_H(v) = |\{e \in E(H) : v \in e\}|$, the number of hyperedges incident to $v$.

title: Minimum Degree
content: Defines `minDegree H` as the infimum of degrees over all vertices appearing in at least one edge. Uses `⨅` (infimum) over the vertex set $\bigcup_{e \in E} e$. The minimum degree is the central quantity in Problem #834: the question asks whether it can reach 7 in 3-critical 3-uniform hypergraphs.
mathContext: $\delta(H) = \min_{v \in V(H)} \deg_H(v)$, where $V(H) = \bigcup_{e \in E(H)} e$.

title: Transversal (Vertex Cover)
content: Defines `IsTransversal H T`: the vertex set $T$ intersects every hyperedge. Also known as a vertex cover or hitting set. The condition $\forall e \in E(H),\, (T \cap e).\text{Nonempty}$ ensures every edge has at least one endpoint in $T$. Finding minimum-size transversals is NP-hard in general, but structural results exist for critical hypergraphs.
mathContext: $T \subseteq V$ is a transversal iff $\forall e \in E(H),\; T \cap e \ne \emptyset$.

title: Transversal Number τ(H)
content: Defines `transversalNumber H` as the infimum of $|T|$ over all transversals $T$. Uses a conditional infimum: for non-transversals, the contribution is $\top$ (infinity), so the infimum picks the minimum size among actual transversals. The transversal number $\tau(H)$ is dual to the matching number $\nu(H)$ via König-type inequalities.
mathContext: $\tau(H) = \min\{|T| : T \text{ is a transversal of } H\}$. For 3-uniform hypergraphs, $\tau(H) \ge 1$.

title: Edge Removal
content: Defines `removeEdge H e`: removes a single edge, giving edge set $E(H) \setminus \{e\}$. Central to criticality definitions—a hypergraph is critical if removing any edge changes the relevant parameter.
mathContext: $H - e = (V, E(H) \setminus \{e\})$.

title: k-Transversal-Criticality
content: Defines `IsTransversalCritical H k`: $\tau(H) = k$ and removing any edge strictly reduces the transversal number. Every edge is 'essential' for maintaining $\tau(H) = k$. For $k = 3$, each edge's removal allows a size-2 cover, meaning each edge contains a pair that blocks all size-2 covers.
mathContext: $H$ is $k$-$\tau$-critical iff $\tau(H) = k$ and $\forall e \in E(H),\; \tau(H - e) < k$.

title: Proper Hypergraph Coloring
content: Defines `IsProperColoring H k c`: $c : V \to \text{Fin}\;k$ is proper if no edge of size $\ge 2$ is monochromatic. For each edge, there must exist two vertices with different colors. For 2-uniform hypergraphs (graphs), this reduces to standard proper coloring. The $|e| \ge 2$ guard handles degenerate singleton edges.
mathContext: $c : V \to [k]$ is proper iff $\forall e \in E(H),\; |e| \ge 2 \Rightarrow \exists v_1, v_2 \in e,\; c(v_1) \ne c(v_2)$.

title: Chromatic Number χ(H)
content: Defines `chromaticNumber H` as the infimum of $k$ admitting a proper $k$-coloring. Uses conditional infimum like `transversalNumber`. 2-colorable hypergraphs ($\chi = 2$) have 'Property B' in the Bernstein/Erdős–Hajnal sense. The chromatic number of hypergraphs generalizes the graph chromatic number.
mathContext: $\chi(H) = \min\{k : \exists c : V \to [k],\; c \text{ is proper}\}$.

title: k-Chromatic-Criticality
content: Defines `IsChromaticCritical H k`: $\chi(H) = k$ and removing any edge strictly reduces the chromatic number. Unlike $\tau$-criticality, $\chi$-criticality allows high minimum degree because coloring constraints are more flexible—many independent vertex sets can share colors without violating the no-monochromatic-edge condition.
mathContext: $H$ is $k$-$\chi$-critical iff $\chi(H) = k$ and $\forall e \in E(H),\; \chi(H - e) < k$.

title: The Transversal Question
content: Formalizes the $\tau$-critical interpretation of Problem #834: does there exist a 3-uniform, 3-$\tau$-critical hypergraph with $\delta(H) \ge 7$? Quantifies over a vertex type $V$ with `Fintype` and `DecidableEq`. Proven FALSE by Li's bound.
mathContext: $\exists H:\; |e| = 3$ for all $e$, $\tau$-critical with $\tau = 3$, $\delta(H) \ge 7$. Answer: NO.

title: The Chromatic Question
content: Formalizes the $\chi$-critical interpretation: does there exist a 3-uniform, 3-$\chi$-critical hypergraph with $\delta(H) \ge 7$? Same existential structure, but with `IsChromaticCritical`. Proven TRUE via Lovász's construction.
mathContext: $\exists H:\; |e| = 3$ for all $e$, $\chi$-critical with $\chi = 3$, $\delta(H) \ge 7$. Answer: YES.

title: Li's Bound (2025)
content: Axiomatizes Li's 2025 result: every 3-uniform, 3-$\tau$-critical hypergraph satisfies $\delta(H) \le 6$. A universal bound with no exceptions. The bound is tight (explicit constructions achieve $\delta = 6$). Li's proof analyzes the structure of critical edge sets and their intersection patterns.
mathContext: $\forall H$ 3-uniform and $\tau$-critical with $\tau = 3$: $\delta(H) \le 6$.

title: Transversal Answer: NO (Proved)
content: Proves `¬transversal_question` by contradiction: assume such a hypergraph exists with $\delta \ge 7$, apply Li's bound to get $\delta \le 6$, derive $7 \le 6$ via `omega`. Complete Lean proof with 0 sorries. Uses `intro` to destructure the existential and `@li_bound` with explicit type class instances.
mathContext: $\neg\exists H:\; \delta(H) \ge 7$ when 3-uniform and $\tau$-critical. Proof: $7 \le \delta(H) \le 6$ is absurd.

title: Lovász's Construction
content: Axiomatizes Lovász's result: for any $d$, there exist 3-uniform, 3-$\chi$-critical hypergraphs with $\delta(H) \ge d$. An unbounded existence result—$\chi$-critical hypergraphs can have arbitrarily high minimum degree. Lovász's constructions use iterated product operations on hypergraphs.
mathContext: $\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \exists H$ 3-uniform and $\chi$-critical with $\chi = 3$ and $\delta(H) \ge d$.

title: Chromatic Answer: YES (Proved)
content: Proves `chromatic_question` by instantiating `lovasz_construction 7`. Uses `obtain` to destructure the existential, then re-packages witnesses with `exact`. Complete Lean proof with 0 sorries.
mathContext: $\exists H:\; \delta(H) \ge 7$ with $\chi$-criticality. Proof: apply Lovász with $d = 7$.

title: Complete Resolution
content: The main theorem `erdos_834_resolution`: $\neg\text{transversal\_question} \land \text{chromatic\_question}$. Pairs `transversal_answer_no` and `chromatic_answer_yes`. Completely resolves Problem #834 for both interpretations, demonstrating that the answer depends fundamentally on the definition of '3-critical'.
mathContext: Problem #834: NO for $\tau$-critical ($\delta \le 6$, Li), YES for $\chi$-critical ($\delta$ unbounded, Lovász).

title: Tightness of Li's Bound
content: Axiomatizes tightness: there exist 3-uniform, 3-$\tau$-critical hypergraphs achieving $\delta(H) = 6$ exactly. Li's bound $\delta \le 6$ cannot be improved. The tight examples are explicit finite constructions that demonstrate the sharpness of the bound.
mathContext: $\exists H$ with $\delta(H) = 6$ that is 3-uniform and $\tau$-critical. So $\max_{H} \delta(H) = 6$.

title: Summary Theorem
content: Combines Li's universal bound and Lovász's universal existence: (1) all 3-uniform $\tau$-critical hypergraphs have $\delta \le 6$, and (2) for any $d$, there exist 3-uniform $\chi$-critical hypergraphs with $\delta \ge d$. Proved directly by pairing the two axioms. Complete picture of minimum degree behavior for both criticality notions.
mathContext: $(\forall H\; \tau\text{-critical}:\; \delta(H) \le 6) \;\land\; (\forall d,\; \exists H\; \chi\text{-critical}:\; \delta(H) \ge d)$.
